Formulation
Predisposing: Family history of migraine; computer-intensive occupation.  
Precipitating: Onset of new work project and possible screen strain.  
Perpetuating: Continued screen exposure, sub-therapeutic analgesic dosing, anxiety about migraines.  
Protective: Good insight, help-seeking behavior, social supports, no psychiatric comorbidity identified.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Probable migraine with associated anxiety
- Patient Goal(s):
  • Obtain effective pain relief  
  • Prevent future severe episodes  
  • Maintain ability to work
- Clinical Goal(s):
  • Achieve acute symptom control; introduce appropriate analgesic regime  
  • Identify and mitigate migraine triggers  
  • Monitor for development of chronic migraine or mood disturbance
- Actions (Patient):
  • Trial prescribed Naproxen (or alternative) as directed  
  • Use headache diary to track triggers, severity, and response to medication  
  • Adjust screen brightness, ensure regular breaks, maintain hydration  
  • Seek review sooner if neurological symptoms develop or pain worsens
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  • Prescribe appropriate NSAID ± Paracetamol/Codeine; provide dosing instructions  
  • Educate on migraine management and trigger identification  
  • Arrange follow-up in 1–2 weeks; consider prophylactic therapy if headaches recur  
  • Advise eye examination if visual strain persists

Secondary Problem: Mild situational stress/anxiety
- Patient Goal(s):
  • Reduce worry about headaches affecting work  
  • Develop coping strategies for work-related stress
- Clinical Goal(s):
  • Screen for anxiety/depression at review  
  • Provide brief stress-management advice
- Actions (Patient):
  • Implement regular breaks, hydration, ergonomic adjustments  
  • Practice relaxation techniques (deep breathing, brief stretches) during work
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  • Provide psycho-education on stress and headache interplay  
  • Offer information on local mindfulness or stress-reduction resources  
  • Reassess mental health symptoms at next appointment

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Correct analgesic dosing, migraine triggers, red-flag symptoms requiring urgent review
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Escalating pain, visual disturbance, focal neurological deficit, persistent vomiting, inability to perform daily tasks
- Coping Strategies: Headache diary, hydration, screen breaks, adequate sleep, relaxation exercises

Consent, Coordination & Review
- Patient Consent to Plan: Yes (verbal)
- Copy of Mental Health Care Plan Given to Patient: Not recorded
- Other Mental Health Professionals Involved in Patient Care: None currently
- GP Acknowledgment (if completed by other MH Professional): Not applicable
- Review Date: Within 1–2 weeks or sooner if deterioration

● Internal conflicts: None noted
